wireframe_control.additive_note: Wireframes are additive: added to the Feature Design Package, never merged into a canonical document, no delta and no version_bump.
wireframe_control.fidelity: low — layout, hierarchy and state, not visual design
wireframe_control.viewport_primary: 360px — the producer is on a phone, per P-01. Desktop is the secondary layout, not the reference one.

screens.name: Producer registration form
screens.layout:
```text
┌─ HarvestLink ─────────────── [account] ┐
│                                        │
│  Register as a producer         1 of 1 │
│                                        │
│  Business name                         │
│  [____________________________]        │
│                                        │
│  Food Business Operator (FBO) number   │
│  [____________________________]        │
│  ⓘ Where do I find this?               │
│  ⚠ field-level error appears here      │
│                                        │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │ ☐  I confirm that I, not       │    │
│  │    HarvestLink, am the Food    │    │
│  │    Business Operator for what  │    │
│  │    I sell here.                │    │
│  │                                │    │
│  │    This is a legal declaration.│    │
│  └────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                        │
│  [ Submit registration ]               │
│                                        │
│  Your details are saved as you type.   │
└────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
design_notes: The attestation is boxed and set apart from the other fields, with its consequence stated in plain words. UJ-01 step 4 warns it must not feel like boilerplate — a tick-box inline with business name would read as terms-and-conditions, and this one carries the facilitation-only regulatory position.
The attestation is NOT pre-ticked and has no 'select all' affordance. A pre-ticked legal declaration is not a declaration.

'Where do I find this?' addresses UJ-01 step 3's abandonment risk directly: the producer who does not have their FBO number to hand is the predicted drop-off, and the cheapest intervention is telling them where to look.
The save-as-you-type line is the visible half of the resumption behaviour UJ-F02 says nothing specifies. Drawn because the journey needs it; flagged below because no acceptance criterion supports it.

states.note: Submit enabled; validation is on submit, not on blur — an outdoor user tabbing through fields should not be scolded mid-entry.
Error sits under the FBO field, names the expected format, and the entered value is preserved. No record is created.
Client-side guard shown, but the screen assumes nothing about it — the server refuses regardless, and the wireframe annotates that the client guard is an affordance, not the control.

screens.name: Registration status
screens.work_unit_note: No Work Unit builds this screen. Drawn anyway, because UJ-01 carries three steps here and a wireframe gap would hide the Work Unit gap. See finding WF-F01.
screens.layout:
```text
┌─ HarvestLink ─────────────── [account] ┐
│                                        │
│  Your registration                     │
│                                        │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────┐    │
│  │  ◐  Checking your FBO number   │    │
│  │                                │    │
│  │  We're confirming your Food    │    │
│  │  Business Operator registration│    │
│  │  with the competent authority. │    │
│  │                                │    │
│  │  Most checks finish within a   │    │
│  │  working day. We'll email you. │    │
│  └────────────────────────────────┘    │
│                                        │
│  What you can do now                   │
│  ✓ Add your business details           │
│  ✓ Draft listings (not published)      │
│  ✗ Publish listings — available once   │
│    your registration is confirmed      │
│                                        │
└────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
design_notes: The blocked action is shown as blocked with its reason, not hidden. UJ-01 step 6 is explicit that a silently absent publish button generates the support contact this screen exists to prevent.

'Most checks finish within a working day' is an expectation, not a commitment, and it is deliberately not a countdown or a progress bar. S-F1.1-b-AC3 means a timeout and a slow answer are indistinguishable to this screen; a progress bar would assert knowledge the system does not have.
The 'what you can do now' list exists because UJ-01 step 5 identifies this as the point where the producer has finished their part and cannot act further. An empty waiting screen is read as failure.

states.note: The only state for both a slow lookup and a timed-out one.
Panel becomes confirmation; publish moves from ✗ to ✓.
Panel states the reason returned by the register and what the producer can do. Publish stays ✗ — see finding WF-F02.

screens.name: Verification outcome email
screens.layout:
```text
┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Subject: Your HarvestLink registration │
│                                        │
│ We couldn't confirm your FBO           │
│ registration.                          │
│                                        │
│ Reason: <reason returned by the        │
│          competent authority>          │
│                                        │
│ Your listings stay unpublished until   │
│ this is resolved.                      │
│                                        │
│ [ View your registration ]             │
└────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
design_notes: Carries no FBO number, no business identifiers and no personal data beyond the addressee. An email is forwarded, quoted and archived outside the platform's control, and a registration number in a subject line is a disclosure nobody authorised.
The reason is passed through from the register rather than paraphrased. A rewritten regulatory reason is a new assertion about a legal status.

states.note: Same template, positive outcome. Drawn once.

not_wireframed.reason: Public landing exists already and is unchanged by this cycle. Redrawing it would put an unchanged screen into an additive folder, where a later reader would take it for a change.
External IdP authentication screen is owned by the identity provider, not by HarvestLink. Wireframing someone else's screen would assert a design this product does not control.

findings.summary: WF-02 is fully specified and has no Work Unit.
findings.detail: The registration status screen carries three journey steps and two acceptance criteria, and nothing in tasks.json builds it. This is UJ-F01 reaching the wireframe stage unresolved, now with a concrete surface attached and therefore a concrete size.
findings.resolution_note: Escalated, not absorbed. The wireframe was drawn rather than omitted so the gap is visible as a missing builder rather than a missing screen.

findings.summary: WF-02's rejected state has nowhere to go.
findings.detail: The rejected panel says what the producer can do, and no acceptance criterion says what that is. S-F1.1-b-AC2 ends at 'notified with the reason'. Whether a producer can correct an FBO number and resubmit, and whether that is a new registration or an amendment, is unspecified.
findings.resolution_note: The wireframe shows the reason and stops. A resubmit button was drawn and removed during authoring — it would have implied a flow with no acceptance criteria, no Work Unit and no verifier behind it.

findings.summary: WF-01's save-as-you-type is drawn but unspecified.
findings.detail: UJ-F02 notes the journey has no resumption path. The wireframe shows one, because a form the persona will abandon needs one. No acceptance criterion covers what is saved, for how long, or whether a partial registration with an unverified FBO number is a record at all — which is a data question (DAT-1.1 owns Producer) as much as a UX one.
findings.resolution_note: Drawn as a line of copy, flagged here, and deliberately not detailed into behaviour.

consistency_check.note: Screen states were checked against the acceptance criteria they claim. One correction during authoring: WF-02's pending panel originally showed a progress bar with an estimated completion time. That contradicts S-F1.1-b-AC3 — the system cannot distinguish a slow lookup from a timed-out one, so a progress bar would display confidence it does not have. Replaced with a non-committal expectation.

artifacts.name: wireframes.md
artifacts.description: 3 low-fidelity screens covering 3 of 5 journey touchpoints and all 6 acceptance criteria with a user-facing surface; 3 findings

content.execution_summary:
• Three low-fidelity screens: the registration form (WF-01), the registration status screen (WF-02) and the verification outcome email (WF-03). Drawn at 360px first, because P-01 is a producer on a phone, often outdoors.
• Two touchpoints were deliberately not wireframed: the public landing is unchanged by this cycle, and the external IdP screen belongs to the identity provider. An unchanged screen placed in an additive folder reads as a change; someone else's screen redrawn here asserts a design this product does not control.
• All 6 acceptance criteria with a user-facing surface are covered. S-F1.1-b-AC4 has no surface and correctly has no screen.
• Two design decisions carry regulatory weight rather than aesthetic weight. The attestation on WF-01 is boxed, unticked, and states that it is a legal declaration — UJ-01 warns it must not feel like boilerplate, and it is what the facilitation-only position rests on. WF-02's pending panel shows no progress bar, because S-F1.1-b-AC3 makes a timeout and a slow answer indistinguishable, and a progress bar would display confidence the system does not possess.
• Three findings, none resolved here. WF-F01 carries UJ-F01 forward with a concrete surface and therefore a concrete size: the status screen is fully specified and no Work Unit builds it. WF-F02 is new — the rejected state tells the producer what happened and nothing specifies what they can do next; a resubmit button was drawn and removed, because it would have implied a flow with no AC, no Work Unit and no verifier. WF-F03 notes the save-as-you-type line is drawn but unspecified, and is a data question as much as a UX one.
• Output is additive: it lands in the FDP's additive/ folder and is never merged.
• Knowledge bases consulted: kb-L1-sdlc-templates (wireframe and state conventions); kb-L2-food-domain through the persona record (FD2 — UI-first, low technical capability, which is why the mobile layout is the reference and not the adaptation).
• Guardrails evaluated: gr-L1-consistency-check (pass — one correction, the removed progress bar).
• tool-L1-figma-create-frame not invoked; it is optional per the BOM row and ASCII wireframes stay readable in a terminal, a diff and a PR review.
